From 000eca5d044d1ee23b4ca311793cf3fc528da6c6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tianyu Li <tianyu.li@arm.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jun 2022 17:32:11 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] mm/mempolicy: fix get_nodes out of bound access

When user specified more nodes than supported, get_nodes will access nmask
array out of bounds.

Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20220601093211.2970565-1-tianyu.li@arm.com
Fixes: e130242dc351 ("mm: simplify compat numa syscalls")
Signed-off-by: Tianyu Li <tianyu.li@arm.com>
Cc: Arnd Bergmann <arnd@arndb.de>
Cc: Mark Rutland <mark.rutland@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/mm/mempolicy.c b/mm/mempolicy.c
index 9689919a2829..f4cd963550c1 100644
--- a/mm/mempolicy.c
+++ b/mm/mempolicy.c
@@ -1388,7 +1388,7 @@ static int get_nodes(nodemask_t *nodes, const unsigned long __user *nmask,
 		unsigned long bits = min_t(unsigned long, maxnode, BITS_PER_LONG);
 		unsigned long t;
 
-		if (get_bitmap(&t, &nmask[maxnode / BITS_PER_LONG], bits))
+		if (get_bitmap(&t, &nmask[(maxnode - 1) / BITS_PER_LONG], bits))
 			return -EFAULT;
 
 		if (maxnode - bits >= MAX_NUMNODES) {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `mm/mempolicy.c`**
- The line of code that accesses the `nmask` array has been modified. 
- The original code accessed `nmask[maxnode / BITS_PER_LONG]`, which could lead to an out-of-bounds access if `maxnode` exceeds the size of the `nmask` array.
- The modified code now accesses `nmask[(maxnode - 1) / BITS_PER_LONG]`, which correctly adjusts the index to prevent out-of-bounds access.

### Relationships
- The change addresses a bug where the `get_nodes` function could access memory outside the bounds of the `nmask` array when the user specifies more nodes than the system supports. 
- This modification is a direct fix to the issue identified in the commit message, which references a previous commit that simplified compatibility for NUMA syscalls, indicating that the bug was introduced during that simplification process.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (maxnode > PAGE_SIZE*BITS_PER_BYTE)
```
```c
if (get_bitmap(&t, &nmask[maxnode / BITS_PER_LONG], bits))
```
Reason:
The first statement checks if the `maxnode` exceeds the maximum allowable size, but it does not prevent the subsequent access to the `nmask` array. The second statement accesses the `nmask` array using an index calculated from `maxnode`, which can lead to an out-of-bounds access if `maxnode` is greater than the actual size of the `nmask` array.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (get_bitmap(&t, &nmask[(maxnode - 1) / BITS_PER_LONG], bits))
```
```c
while (maxnode > MAX_NUMNODES) {
```
Reason:
The first statement adjusts the index calculation to use `(maxnode - 1)`, ensuring that the access to the `nmask` array remains within valid bounds. The second statement ensures that the loop only processes nodes that are within the supported range, preventing any out-of-bounds access when `maxnode` exceeds `MAX_NUMNODES`.
